manifest.purpose: Secure drop-in replacement for inputs/cbc_unpad.cpp. Keeps exact signature `void pad_check(const unsigned char block[16], int *valid, int *unpadded_len)`, no namespaces/overloads, pure C++11, no dynamic allocation/STL/exceptions. Reads last byte n=block[15]; computes len_ok = (n>=1 && n<=16) via arithmetic (no early branch skipping the scan). For all 16 positions i=0..15, unconditionally computes whether position i is 'within the last n bytes' (i >= 16-n, using a clamped/safe start even when n is out of 1..16 range by treating n as clamped to compute a boolean mask) and whether block[i]==n, combining into a per-position 'this position matches expected pad value OR is outside the padding region' boolean using bitwise (&,|,^) operators only -- never && / || / early return/break inside the loop. Accumulate a single running int mismatch flag via bitwise OR across all 16 iterations (fixed trip-count for loop, no data-dependent bound). After the fixed-length loop, compute final validity = len_ok & !mismatch via bitwise ops, then use exactly one branch at the very end (not inside the loop, so it does not affect the loop's iteration count) to write *valid and *unpadded_len (16-n if valid else 16). This final branch is after all scanning work is already uniformly done for every call, satisfying SR1/SR3. Matches reference truth table for FR1-FR4/SR2 exactly. This is the file graded in place by the evaluator's compile_and_run harness.
